# Authorization & Privilege-Escalation Checklist: Role-Based Access for Users

**Purpose**: Author self-check of `spec.md` requirements quality before starting `/speckit-tasks` / `/speckit-implement` — focused on the highest-risk area of this feature: who can grant/revoke which standing, cross-tenant boundaries, and privilege-escalation edge cases.
**Created**: 2026-08-17
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Is it specified whether a Tenant Admin can revoke their own Tenant Admin standing, and if so what their access becomes immediately afterward? [Gap, Spec §FR-005(c)] — Resolved 2026-08-17: FR-005(c) now says "including their own"; User Story 2 scenario 12 added.
- [x] CHK002 Is it specified whether granting Tenant Admin standing to a user requires that user to already hold membership in that tenant, or could it implicitly create membership? [Gap, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-005(c)] — Resolved: FR-005(c) requires existing membership; non-member grant is rejected (404), User Story 2 scenario 10.
- [x] CHK003 Is there a requirement (or explicit non-requirement) for audit logging of standing grant/revoke actions — who performed it, on whom, when — given this is a privilege-escalation-sensitive feature? [Gap, Non-Functional] — Resolved: Assumptions now explicitly declares audit logging out of scope, consistent with the platform's existing no-logging baseline.
- [x] CHK004 Is there a requirement stating how quickly a revoked user's *already-issued* session loses the revoked standing (immediately on their next request, vs. up to the token's remaining lifetime)? [Gap, Non-Functional, Spec §SC-004/§SC-008] — Resolved: new FR-015 + SC-010.
- [x] CHK005 Is a not-found case specified for granting/revoking standing against a `userId` or tenant-member pair that doesn't exist? [Gap, Spec §FR-005(c)/§FR-014] — Resolved: FR-014 and FR-005(c) both specify not-found behavior; contracts/openapi.yaml 404 responses added.

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK006 Is "platform-wide" for System Admin (FR-008) precise enough to rule out any per-tenant exception, given FR-006 separately restricts Tenant Admin standing to the tenant it was granted for? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006 vs §FR-008] — Resolved: FR-008 now states FR-006 applies only to Tenant Admin standing.
- [x] CHK007 Do FR-005(c) and FR-014 specify what happens if a caller grants standing to a user who already holds it, or revokes standing from a user who doesn't hold it (no-op vs. error)? [Clarity, Gap, Spec §FR-005(c)/§FR-014] — Resolved: both now specify idempotent no-op.
- [x] CHK008 Is the difference in requirement strength between FR-004's "MAY additionally be performed" and FR-005(b)'s "MUST allow" for the same Tenant-update capability intentional, or an inconsistency to resolve? [Clarity, Consistency, Spec §FR-004 vs §FR-005] — Resolved: FR-004 changed to "MUST additionally be allowed."

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK009 Do FR-014 ("grant... to **another** user" / "revoke **another** user's...") and User Story 1 acceptance scenario 9 (explicitly "including by that user themselves") contradict each other on whether self-revocation is in scope? [Conflict, Spec §FR-014 vs User Story 1 scenario 9] — Resolved: FR-014 rewritten to explicitly permit self-targeting, matching scenario 9.
- [x] CHK010 Does FR-005(c)'s "grant or revoke Tenant Admin standing for **another** member" carry the same self-targeting ambiguity as FR-014, and is it resolved consistently with whatever FR-014 resolves to? [Conflict, Spec §FR-005(c) vs §FR-014] — Resolved: FR-005(c) now also explicitly permits self-targeting ("including their own"), consistent with FR-014.
- [x] CHK011 Is the decision that Tenant Admin standing needs no "last Tenant Admin" protection (unlike System Admin's FR-011) stated in `spec.md` itself, or only in a downstream planning artifact? [Traceability, Gap, Spec §FR-011] — Resolved: promoted to a spec.md Assumptions bullet, cross-referenced from data-model.md.
- [x] CHK012 Do User Story 1/2's mixed terminology — "grant"/"revoke" (FR-005(c), FR-014) vs. "promoted"/"demoted" (User Story 1 title context, User Story 2 scenario 1) — refer to the same action consistently, or could a reader treat them as distinct concepts? [Consistency, Terminology] — Resolved: User Story 2 scenario 1 normalized to "granted Tenant Admin standing"; remaining informal "demoted" instances are already directly cross-referenced to FR-014 in the same sentence.

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK013 Is SC-008's "effect immediately observable" measurable without specifying *whose* next observation counts (the granter's UI, or the target's own next authenticated request)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-008] — Resolved: SC-008 now names both the granter's view and the affected user's next request (per FR-015).
- [x] CHK014 Is SC-007 ("any attempt to remove the platform's last System Admin is blocked 100% of the time") verifiable independent of whether the attempt is a revoke (FR-014) or an account deletion, given both are named in FR-011? [Measurability, Spec §SC-007 vs §FR-011] — Resolved: SC-007 now names both trigger paths and concurrent attempts explicitly.

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK015 Is there an acceptance scenario for a Tenant Admin attempting to grant Tenant Admin standing to a user who is not yet a member of their tenant at all? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §User Story 2] — Resolved: User Story 2 scenario 10 added.
- [x] CHK016 Is there an acceptance scenario confirming that a newly-promoted user's *own* very next request reflects their new standing (not just the granter's observation, per SC-004/SC-008)? [Coverage, Gap] — Resolved: User Story 2 scenario 11 added.
- [x] CHK017 Is there a scenario or note addressing a user who holds both System Admin standing and Tenant Admin standing for a specific tenant simultaneously — does anything behave differently, or is the Tenant Admin flag simply redundant-but-harmless there? [Coverage, Gap] — Resolved: new Assumptions bullet ("redundant but harmless").

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK018 Is behavior specified for two concurrent revoke requests against the platform's last two remaining System Admins (a race that could leave zero if both checks read the count before either write commits)? [Edge Case, Gap] — Resolved: FR-011 now requires atomic enforcement; research.md §9 documents the locking-read implementation approach.
- [x] CHK019 Is behavior specified for revoking a user's Tenant Admin standing concurrently with removing that same user's membership in the same tenant? [Edge Case, Gap] — Resolved: new Assumptions bullet — both orders converge on the same safe end state.
- [x] CHK020 Is the last-remaining-System-Admin edge case (Edge Cases section) explicitly cross-referenced to both trigger paths (FR-014 revoke, and account deletion), or does a reader have to infer the account-deletion path applies too? [Edge Case, Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases vs §FR-011] — Already satisfied: the Edge Cases bullet already names both "FR-014's revoke capability... or have their account removed."

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK021 Is there a requirement (or explicit non-requirement) limiting how many users may simultaneously hold System Admin standing? [Gap, Non-Functional] — Resolved: Assumptions states no upper bound.
- [x] CHK022 Is there a requirement (or explicit non-requirement) for rate-limiting or throttling repeated grant/revoke attempts, given they are privilege-sensitive actions? [Gap, Non-Functional] — Resolved: Assumptions states explicitly out of scope.

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK023 Is the Assumption that "a Tenant Admin can only ever create more Tenant Admins within their own tenant, never grant System Admin standing" cross-checked against FR-005's explicit scope (which never mentions System Admin) to confirm no code path could conflate the two? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions vs §FR-005] — Resolved: FR-005 now explicitly states it "never grants any System Admin capability (see FR-002/FR-014)."
- [x] CHK024 Is the dependency on `GET /api/users` (or equivalent existing-user lookup, referenced implicitly by User Story 2 scenario 1's "existing user") stated as an explicit requirement anywhere in the Functional Requirements list, or only implied by acceptance-scenario wording? [Dependency, Gap, Spec §FR-005(a)] — Resolved: new FR-016.

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK025 Is there any remaining ambiguity about whether "another user"/"another member" (FR-005(c), FR-014) is meant literally (excludes self) or loosely (typical case, not a hard exclusion) — given the acceptance scenarios lean one way for System Admin and are silent for Tenant Admin? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-005(c)/§FR-014] — Resolved: same fix as CHK009/CHK010 — both FRs now explicitly include self-targeting.
- [x] CHK026 Is there a requirement & acceptance-criteria ID scheme consistently applied to every privilege-escalation-relevant requirement (FR-001, FR-005, FR-006, FR-008, FR-009, FR-011, FR-014) so each is independently traceable and testable? [Traceability] — Already satisfied: every FR (now through FR-016) has a unique, stable ID.
